title: Midnight ldconfig & NVML trace journal
content:
Purpose: capture a late-night, stepwise attempt to reproduce a sporadic GPU OOM that seems tied to library load order (ld.so/ldconfig shims) + NVML driver quirk. This is a personal scratchpad — rough chronology, commands I ran, small diffs, and hypotheses for next steps.

---

Context summary:
- Host: rwd-inf-gpu-07 (internal in eu-west1)
- GPU: A100-SXM4 40GB, driver: 535.86, CUDA toolkit installed: 12.2 (multiple conflicting libs in /usr/local/cuda and /opt/cuda-11.8)
- Symptoms: intermittent CUDA out-of-memory during long autoregressive sampling jobs after ~200-400 steps; short jobs (<100 tokens) always OK. Reboot sometimes fixes for a day.
- Suspected surface issue: mixed libcuda/compat layers present, ldconfig cache changes when we deploy a shim (we use an LD_PRELOAD shim for a mem-tracker). NVML reports GPU memory as free but kernels OOM.

Repro attempts (timestamps local):

2026-03-04 23:40 — baseline small repro (works)
- command: python -u small_repro.py --model tiny --tokens 50
- output: completes, no OOM

23:58 — longer run to try to trigger OOM
- command: python -u sample_long.py --model rwd-7b -n 600 --batch 1
- 00:06:23 crash: Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "sample_long.py", line 412, in <module>
      out = model.generate(input, max_new_tokens=600)
  torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 32.00 GiB (GPU 0; 39.45 GiB total capacity; 28.14 GiB already allocated; 9.87 GiB free; 24.36 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
- nvml for that PID showed: free ~= 10 GiB; nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo returned total=40960MB, free=10240MB
- but nvidia-smi -q showed no large consumers besides our PID

Hypothesis notes:
- Hypothesis A: fragmentation of the device-resident KV cache across repeated forward/backward leads to large reserved pool reported by torch, but kernel still fails when attempting a transient allocation. That is normal, but why does it only fail on some runs?
- Hypothesis B: LD_PRELOAD shim (libmempeek.so) that hooks malloc/cudaMalloc and injects bookkeeping in our Docker image might change allocator behavior and cause different alignment/fragmentation patterns leading to OOM.
- Hypothesis C: mismatched libcuda (from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu) vs driver-bindings from our packaged CUDA toolkit (embedding a different cuda runtime) cause intermittent failures when driver exposes different NVML semantics under heavy load.

Commands & traces I collected:

1) ldd of python binary within container image (to catch mixed libs):
- docker exec -it rwd-runner ldd /usr/bin/python3 | egrep -i "cuda|nvidia|nvml|libcudart|libcuda" || true
  -> libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (driver package)
  -> libcudart.so.12 => /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12 (toolkit in image)
  -> libnvidia-ml.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1

Observation: both driver-provided libcuda and toolkit-provided libcudart coexist (expected), but need to ensure loader picks the driver libcuda at runtime. Sometimes containers have a stale /usr/local/cuda/lib64 added earlier in LD_LIBRARY_PATH.

2) ldconfig -p | egrep -i "libcuda|libcudart|libnvidia-ml"
- shows two entries for libcudart (12 and 11) pointing to /opt/cuda-11.8/lib64 and /usr/local/cuda/lib64.
- ran: sudo ldconfig && sudo ldconfig -p > /tmp/ldcache-before.txt
- then toggled: rename /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12 -> libcudart.so.12.disabled and ran ldconfig to force loader to prefer /opt/cuda-11.8 libs.

3) NVML tracing (attempt to capture nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo semantics):
- I launched a small C shim that calls nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo in a tight loop for the PID of the python job and logs values pre/post crash. Pseudocommand: ./nvml-poll --pid 21345 --interval 0.5 --out nvml-trace.log
- nvml-trace.log around crash: entries show free memory drop from 12.1 GiB -> 9.9 GiB then some momentary spikes showing free==~20 GiB for a single poll, then back to ~9-10 GiB. That spike is suspicious (possibly probing race where driver reports changed memory due to migration between CUDA contexts).

4) strace on process (short run to capture open/ld.so activity):
- sudo strace -ff -p <pid> -e trace=open,openat,read,write 2>/tmp/strace-pid.log
- grep for libcudart/libcuda loads: saw occasional open("/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12", O_RDONLY) and also opens for /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1. Might be different library handles resolved by dlopen at different times.

5) reproducing with LD_PRELOAD off vs on:
- baseline: LD_PRELOAD=/opt/shims/libmempeek.so python sample_long.py -> crashed at step ~360
- with LD_PRELOAD unset: python sample_long.py -> completed once (weird), then second run crashed. Inconsistent.

6) PyTorch caching behavior:
- torch.cuda.memory_summary() before crash shows large reserved blocks; after clearing caches (torch.cuda.empty_cache()) run continued longer in one attempt. I added periodic empty_cache() in a patched script which reduced immediate OOMs but did not eliminate failures after many steps.

Small diffs I captured (git-ish notes):
- build/container: changed LD_LIBRARY_PATH in Dockerfile between builds: +/usr/local/cuda/lib64 vs removed. That correlates with some days of stability.
- kernel: upgraded from 6.1.0-12 to 6.1.0-14 around Feb 2026; not directly correlated but worth noting.

Quick experiments to try next (ordered):
1) Force loader to use driver libcuda only: in container, set LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu and remove /usr/local/cuda from image path. Re-run long sampling 5x.
2) Rebuild mem-tracker shim without hooking cudaMalloc (only host malloc) to see if cuda call interception changes behavior.
3) Add NVML-based sampling to detect transient spikes: poll NVML at 100ms and correlate with OOM timestamp to see if spikes precede crash.
4) Try running identical workload under a different driver version (540.x) on a canary host to see if frequency changes. (Need infra ticket to schedule.)
5) Capture coredump of python process on OOM (set ulimit -c unlimited, ensure container allows core dumps) and inspect with gdb to see failing allocation site.

Notes on what looked weird and may be unique:
- the NVML spike (free memory suddenly reported much larger for one poll) — suggests either driver-side accounting glitch or multiple contexts moving memory between processes (e.g., CUDA peer access or MIG-like behavior).
- ldconfig entries for multiple libcudart versions may cause mixing of runtimes; while mixing libcudart is usually OK when libcuda is the single driver provider, the coexistence seems to change behavior when our shim is present.

Hypothesis refinement:
- Primary: Our LD_PRELOAD shim alters memory allocation alignment leading to more fragmentation; in presence of mixed libcudart versions the runtime occasionally loads a different allocator path causing a transient attempt to allocate very large contiguous block that fails.
- Secondary: Driver NVML reports are momentarily inconsistent during context migration/GC and our process' view (via cuda runtime) is stale leading to mis-estimation of available device memory.

Quick checklist to capture on next failure (what to collect immediately):
- nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nvidia-q.xml
- nvml trace (100ms) starting 2 minutes before job and 2 minutes after crash
- python process pid and lsof -p <pid> to capture loaded libs
- output of ldconfig -p and echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside container
- dmesg | tail -n 200 to see any kernel driver errors
- torch.cuda.memory_summary() dump into a file before exit handler (try/except around generate loop)

Conversation notes to ping others:
- @Marcus: can you try running same job on rwd-canary-gpu-02 (driver 540.x) and report crash frequency?
- @Priya: wondering if the mem-tracker shim is necessary in the Docker image — can we produce equivalent telemetry via nsenter + nvidia-smi polling instead?

Misc commands (copied from session):
- docker exec -it runner /bin/bash -c 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH; python sample_long.py'
- sudo rename -n 's/libcudart.so.12/libcudart.so.12.disabled/' /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12 || true
- ./nvml-poll --pid 21345 --interval 0.1 --out nvml-100ms.log &
- gdb --batch -ex 'attach 21345' -ex 'thread apply all bt' -ex 'detach' -ex 'quit' > /tmp/gdb-backtrace.txt || true

Open questions / to decide:
- Is there a reproducible minimal program that consistently OOMs in the presence of the shim but not without? If yes, we can reduce to a deterministic test.
- Can infra schedule a quick driver rollback to 540.x on one node for A/B? If not, can we get access to canary nodes?

Conclusion (for now): the issue looks like an intersection of allocator fragmentation (PyTorch + shim) and inconsistent runtime/driver library resolution. The next useful experiment is to force the loader to use a single known-good runtime (driver libs only), run the patched script with periodic empty_cache() removed, and collect high-resolution NVML traces. If that increases crash frequency, we have a strong signal for allocator vs loader interplay.

If this helps anyone: I will drop the nvml-trace.log and strace snippets in the infra-debug slack thread and tag Marcus/Priya. Will update this note after the A/B runs.

End of scratchpad (for now).
